# Adjudication Task — Chapter 171

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃171화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|카랑카랑한 목소리의 주인공은 작달막한 노인이었다.
  6|
  7|요즘 초등학생들보다 작은 키에, 꾀죄죄한 옷차림. 그리고 무엇보다…….
  8|
  9|‘엄청 늙었네.’
 10|
 11|내가 오래 산 건 아니지만, 살다 살다 저렇게 늙은 사람은 처음 본다.
 12|
 13|그런 생각을 하고 있는데 갑자기 노인과 내 시선이 딱 마주쳤다.
 14|
 15|“마!”
 16|
 17|“예?”
 18|
 19|“어른이 물었으면 대답을 해야 할 거 아니야. 여기 장 노인 댁 맞아?”
 20|
 21|짬에서 나오는 바이브인가.
 22|
 23|분명 곧 죽을 것 같은 노인인데, 눈빛은 생생하다 못해 형형하다. 나는 묘하게 위축되는 것을 느끼며 대답했다.
 24|
 25|“맞는데요.”
 26|
 27|내 바짓가랑이를 붙잡고 있던 장태보가 엉거주춤 일어났다.
 28|
 29|노인정 친구인가 싶었는데 경계하는 표정을 보니 그런 건 아닌 듯싶다.
 30|
 31|“뉘시오?”
 32|
 33|“지나가던 과객. 그쪽이 장 노인 맞소?”
 34|
 35|“그렇소만.”
 36|
 37|“그렇구려. 혹시나 싶어서 들러 봤소.”
 38|
 39|주위를 쓱 둘러본 노인이 한마디를 덧붙였다.
 40|
 41|“뭐, 딱히 그럴 필요도 없었겠지만.”
 42|
 43|“……?”
 44|
 45|“……?”
 46|
 47|“그럼 이만 가 보지. 일 끝나면 저쪽 사는 꼬맹이 집에 한 번 들르시오. 걱정하고 있으니까.”
 48|
 49|노인은 그렇게 한마디를 툭 던지고 등을 돌렸다.
 50|
 51|저 노인네, 도대체 뭐야?
 52|
 53|도무지 종잡을 수 없는 말과 행동에 모두가 어리둥절해하는 그때, 옆에 있던 청풍이 내 옆구리를 쿡쿡 찔렀다.
 54|
 55|“쩝쩝. 은인. 저분, 좀 이상하지 않아요?”
 56|
 57|“……내 눈에는 당신이 더 이상해. 그리고 입에 든 거나 마저 삼키고 말해요.”
 58|
 59|이 자식은 만두 몇 개를 언제까지 씹는 거야. 만두가 계속 나오는 화수분이라도 갖고 있나?
 60|
 61|내 잔소리에 입 안에 든 것을 꿀꺽 삼킨 청풍이 중얼거렸다.
 62|
 63|“아닌데. 뭔가 이상한데.”
 64|
 65|“그러니까 뭐가?”
 66|
 67|“잘 모르겠어요. 그냥 느낌이 그래요.”
 68|
 69|“그런 말이 어디 있…….”
 70|
 71|잠깐. 그냥 느낌이 그렇다고?
 72|
 73|순간 멈칫했다. 청풍이 그저 그런 괴짜였다면 모를까, 그는 검성의 모든 것을 물려받은 제자이자 나보다 훨씬 윗줄의 절정 고수다.
 74|
 75|어쩌면 저 노인에게서 내가 모르는 뭔가를 느낀 것이 아닐까?
 76|
 77|‘겉으로 봐서는 별다를 게 없는 노인인데…….’
 78|
 79|어차피 밑져야 본전이다. 무슨 일이 벌어져도 이상하지 않은 무림에서는 돌다리도 두드려 보고 건너야지.
 80|
 81|‘기감 발동.’
 82|
 83|띠링.
 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|- 스킬, [기감]을 사용하셨습니다.
 88|
 89|- 최대 90레벨 이하, 70장 이내의 대상을 탐색할 수 있습니다.
 90|
 91|- 범위에 비례해 공력이 소모됩니다.
 92|
 93|
 94|
 95|슈우우욱.
 96|
 97|오직 내 눈에만 보이는 푸른 선이 빠르게 뻗어 나간다.
 98|
 99|가장 가까이에 있던 청풍과 혁무진, 장태보를 통과한 선이 마침내 천천히 멀어져 가는 노인의 등에 닿았다.
100|
101|새하얗게 샌 그의 머리 위로 반투명한 홀로그램 창이 불쑥 솟구친다.
102|
103|
104|
105|[Lv.3 적천강]
106|
107|
108|
109|적천강? 이름 하나는 최종 보스급인데.
110|
111|그러나 멋들어진 이름과는 달리 레벨은 형편없이 낮다. 저 노인은 무공을 익히지 않은 양민이 확실했다.
112|
113|“그냥 헛다리 짚은 것 같은……데.”
114|
115|저절로 말꼬리가 흐려졌다.
116|
117|어느새 휘적휘적 걸어가던 노인의 발걸음이 멈춰 있었기 때문이다.
118|
119|이내 작달막한 체구가 천천히 돌아선다. 십여 장 너머, 묘하게 빛나는 그의 눈빛에 살이 따끔거렸다.
120|
121|‘뭐지?’
122|
123|몸이 덜컥 굳는다. 심장이 빠르게 뛰고 손끝이 움찔거렸다.
124|
125|다음 순간, 노인의 입술이 열리지 않았다면 당장 인벤토리에서 무기를 소환했을지도 몰랐다.
126|
127|“이거 참…….”
128|
129|나를 바라보는 노인의 주름진 입가가 실룩인다. 낮게 가라앉은 목소리가 귓가를 파고들었다.
130|
131|“재미있는 놈일세.”
132|
133|
134|
135|* * *
136|
137|
138|
139|노인, 적천강은 목적지에 도착하자마자 제법 흥미로운 상황에 직면했다.
140|
141|‘오호, 이놈들 보게나.’
142|
143|초절정의 경지는 무신(武神)이라 불려도 손색이 없는 인외의 영역. 그는 한눈에 젊은 놈들의 무위를 알아봤다.
144|
145|한 놈은 그저 그랬지만 다른 두 놈은…… 솔직히 감탄했다.
146|
147|‘저 새파란 나이에 벽을 넘었단 말이지.’
148|
149|특히 어른 앞에서 버릇없게 만두를 쩝쩝대고 있는 저놈은 이미 완숙한 절정의 경지에 다다랐다고 해도 과언이 아니다.
150|
151|과거 몇 번 스치듯이 만났던 구파일방의 장로들 정도는 되어야 견줄 수 있을까?
152|
153|반면에 훌쩍 키가 크고 덩치가 있는 다른 놈은…….
154|
155|‘저, 저 눈깔 싸가지 없게 뜨는 것 보소. 확 파 버릴라.’
156|
157|산송장이라도 본 것 같은 얼굴이다. 그러나 저놈 역시 나이와는 어울리지 않는 무공의 소유자임이 분명했다.
158|
159|‘또래 중에서는 당해 낼 놈이 없겠어.’
160|
161|장강후랑추전랑(長江後浪推前浪).
162|
163|장강의 뒷물결이 앞물결을 밀어 낸다고 했다. 적천강은 문득 새로운 물결이 제법 크고, 거세다는 것을 깨달았다.
164|
165|장강 전체를 집어삼킬 만큼.
166|
167|‘만년한철이니 어쩌니 떠들어 댈 때부터 짐작은 했지만…… 생각 이상으로 흥미로운 놈들일세그려.’
168|
169|수십 장 밖의 기척도 감지해 내는 적천강이다. 그는 장 씨의 집을 나선 순간부터 그들의 대화를 듣고 있었다.
170|
171|장 씨가 우려하는 일이 일어나지 않았다는 사실도 알았다.
172|
173|핍박은커녕, 오히려 저 장 노인이라는 자가 매달리는 모양새였다.
174|
175|‘저 성취에 만년한철까지 가져올 정도면 구파일방? 뭐, 어쨌든 명문 정파 소속인 건 확실해 보이는군.’
176|
177|적천강의 흥미는 딱 거기까지였다. 굳이 저 어린놈들과 인연을 맺을 이유도 없을뿐더러, 정체를 드러내고 싶지도 않았다.
178|
179|이만하면 얻어먹은 밥값으로 충분하니 이 길로 떠날 생각이었다.
180|
181|“그럼 이만 가 보지. 일 끝나면 저쪽 사는 꼬맹이 집에 한 번 들르시오. 걱정하고 있으니까.”
182|
183|적천강은 마지막 말을 툭 던지고 돌아섰다.
184|
185|이미 시간을 상당히 지체했다. 그는 오늘 중으로 태원(太原)에 당도해 하오문에 들를 생각이었다.
186|
187|물론 정체가 알려지는 건 사양이다.
188|
189|‘대충 복면이라도 두르고 윽박지르면 술술 불겠지.’
190|
191|그러나 적천강의 상념은 더 이상 이어지지 못했다.
192|
193|다음 순간, 알 수 없는 뭔가가 그의 뒤에서 쏘아졌기 때문이었다.
194|
195|슈우우욱.
196|
197|보이지도, 들리지도 않는다.
198|
199|다만 느꼈을 뿐이다. 적천강은 등을 파고드는 서늘하고 낯선 뭔가를 느꼈다.
200|
201|‘암습?’
202|
203|아니다. 끈적끈적하고 불쾌한 살기는 느껴지지 않았다.
204|
205|오히려 저 멀리서 바람이 불어오는 것처럼 자연스러웠고, 그래서 더더욱 이질적이었다.
206|
207|미지의 기운은 적천강의 등에 닿자마자 사라졌다.
208|
209|‘이게 무슨.’
210|
211|백여 년에 가까운 세월을 살아온 그였지만 이런 경우는 처음이다.
212|
213|황당해하던 그는 뒤를 돌자마자 범인의 정체를 알 수 있었다.
214|
215|“그냥 헛다리 짚은 것 같은……데.”
216|
217|눈을 마주치자마자 딱 다물리는 입. 흔들리는 눈동자와 움찔거리는 손끝.
218|
219|범인을 바라보던 적천강의 입꼬리가 슬며시 위로 솟구쳤다.
220|
221|“이것 참…….”
222|
223|적천강은 흥미로운 표정으로 턱을 쓰다듬었다.
224|
225|“재미있는 놈일세.”
226|
227|동시에 그의 발이 지면을 밀었다.
228|
229|다음 순간, 그들 사이에 있던 십여 장의 거리가 사라졌다. 적천강이 진태경의 귓가에 속삭였다.
230|
231|
232|
233|* * *
234|
235|
236|
237|인벤토리 소환.
238|
239|딱 여섯 글자다. 창의 이미지를 떠올리며 마음속으로 외치기만 하면 된다. 그런데…….
240|
241|“너, 뭐 하는 놈이냐?”
242|
243|목덜미를 간질이는 숨결에 전신의 털이 쭈뼛 섰다.
244|
245|도대체 언제?
246|
247|아니, 그 전에 어떻게?
248|
249|‘분명히, 분명히 3레벨이었는데.’
250|
251|믿기지 않는 현실이다.
252|
253|곧 죽어도 이상하지 않을 것 같은 노인, 적천강은 내가 지금까지 본 누구보다 빨랐다.
254|
255|감히 대항할 엄두조차 나지 않을 정도로.
256|
257|“마, 어른이 물었으면 답을 해야 할 거 아냐.”
258|
259|“예, 예?”
260|
261|“그게 대답이냐?”
262|
263|빼빼 마르고 주름진 손가락이 가슴을 명치를 쿡쿡 찌른다. 분명 아무런 힘도, 공력도 실리지 않았건만 누군가 검으로 쑤시는 것 같다.
264|
265|“너, 뭐냐고.”
266|
267|나는 마른침을 삼켰다. 입 안은 모래라도 한 움큼 들어간 것처럼 삭막했다.
268|
269|“진태경인데요.”
270|
271|“그딴 거 말고. 어느 문파의 제자냐?”
272|
273|“태원, 태원진가요.”
274|
275|“태원진가? 혹시 사마외도냐?”
276|
277|하마터면 나도 모르게 고개를 끄덕일 뻔했다.
278|
279|사마외도를 언급할 때 노인네의 번뜩이던 눈빛을 보니 실수로라도 그렇다고 대답했다간 즉시 요절을 낼 모양새다.
280|
281|“저, 정파인데요.”
282|
283|“정파 맞아? 근데 말을 왜 더듬어?”
284|
285|“진짭니다.”
286|
287|“그래? 태원진가라…… 들어 본 것 같기도 하고. 아닌 것 같기도 하고.”
288|
289|골똘히 생각에 잠겨 있던 적천강이 문득 나를 묘한 눈빛으로 바라본다.
290|
291|“볼수록 요상한 놈일세. 방금 그거, 너 맞지?”
292|
293|방금 그거?
294|
295|두루뭉술한 말이었지만 바로 알아들을 수 있었다.
296|
297|이 영감, [기감]을 느낀 것이 분명하다.
298|
299|‘이게 말이 되나.’
300|
301|곧장 반응이 오는 것을 보고 어렴풋이 짐작은 했지만, 순간 눈앞이 아득해진다. 세상에, 기감을 감지해 내는 괴물이라니.
302|
303|“왜 대답이 없어?”
304|
305|나는 아랫입술을 질끈 깨물고 대답했다.
306|
307|“아닌데요.”
308|
309|“뭔 줄 알고?”
310|
311|“…….”
312|
313|“마, 너 맞지?”
314|
315|“아닙니다. 아무튼 저 아닙니다.”
316|
317|“오, 뚝심 있어 보이고 좋구먼. 사내다워.”
318|
319|적천강이 허허 웃으며 말을 이었다.
320|
321|“몇 군데 부러뜨리고 다시 물어볼까?”
322|
323|“접니다! 저 맞아요!”
324|
325|“그래. 좋아. 그럼 내게 무슨 짓을 한 거지?”
326|
327|나는 잠시 머뭇거렸다.
328|
329|상대는 살아온 세월만큼이나 눈치가 비상한 노인네다. 여기서 거짓말을 쳤다가 걸리는 날에는 몸 성히 못 돌아간다.
330|
331|최대한 사실에 입각해서, 기분 좋게 전달해야 했다.
332|
333|“범상치 않으신 분 같아 그냥 조금…….”
334|
335|“조금?”
336|
337|“무공을 익히셨는지 본 건데요.”
338|
339|“어떻게?”
340|
341|“예?”
342|
343|“그걸 어떻게 한 것이냐 묻는 것이다.”
344|
345|“그냥, 제 기운을 조금 쏘아 보내서 상대의 기운을 읽는. 뭐 그런 건데요.”
346|
347|“허허. 그래?”
348|
349|재미있다는 듯 웃던 적천강이 주먹을 움켜쥐었다.
350|

Jeok Cheongang tossed out those final words and turned away.

[P87]
He had already wasted a considerable amount of time. He intended to reach Taiyuan before the day was out and pay a visit to the Lower District Sect.

[P88]
Of course, he had no intention of letting anyone discover his identity.

[P89]
*If I wrap a mask around my face and threaten them a little, they should spill everything.*

[P90]
But Jeok Cheongang’s train of thought went no further.

[P91]
The next moment, something unknown shot toward him from behind.

[P92]
Whoosh.

[P93]
He could neither see nor hear it.

[P94]
He merely felt it—a cold, unfamiliar presence closing in on his back.

[P95]
*An ambush?*

[P96]
No. He sensed none of the sticky, unpleasant killing intent that accompanied one.

[P97]
Instead, it felt as natural as a breeze blowing from afar, which only made it more alien.

[P98]
The unknown energy vanished the moment it touched Jeok Cheongang’s back.

[P99]
*What in the world…?*

[P100]
He had lived for nearly a hundred years, yet this was the first time he had ever experienced anything like it.

[P101]
Still bewildered, he turned around and immediately identified the culprit.

[P102]
“Looks like you were just barking up the wrong tree…”

[P103]
The young man’s mouth snapped shut the instant their eyes met. His gaze wavered, and his fingertips twitched.

[P104]
As Jeok Cheongang stared at the culprit, the corners of his mouth slowly rose.

[P105]
“Well, now…”

[P106]
He stroked his chin, intrigued.

[P107]
“What an interesting fellow.”

[P108]
At the same time, his foot pushed off the ground.

[P109]
In the next instant, the distance of more than ten jang between them vanished. Jeok Cheongang whispered into Jin Taekyung’s ear.

[P110]
* * *

[P111]
*Inventory summon.*

[P112]
Just six syllables.

[P113]
All I had to do was picture the spear and shout the words in my mind. But…

[P114]
“What are you?”

[P115]
The breath tickling the back of my neck made every hair on my body stand on end.

[P116]
*When did he—?*

[P117]
No, before that…

[P118]
*How?*

[P119]
*He was definitely, definitely Level 3.*

[P120]
It was impossible to believe.

[P121]
Jeok Cheongang looked as though he could drop dead at any moment, yet he was faster than anyone I had ever seen.

[P122]
So fast that I did not even dare consider resisting him.

[P123]
“Hey. When an elder asks you a question, you’re supposed to answer.”

[P124]
“Y-Yes?”

[P125]
“You call that an answer?”

[P126]
A thin, wrinkled finger repeatedly poked me in the solar plexus. There was no force or internal energy behind it, yet it felt as though someone were stabbing me with a sword.

[P127]
“I’m asking what you are.”

[P128]
I swallowed hard. My mouth felt as dry as if someone had poured a handful of sand into it.

[P129]
“I’m Jin Taekyung.”

[P130]
“Not that crap. Which sect are you a disciple of?”

[P131]
“Taiyuan—the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P132]
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan? Are you one of those demonic, heterodox sorts?”

[P133]
I nearly nodded without thinking.

[P134]
The old man’s eyes had flashed when he mentioned demonic, heterodox arts. If I said yes even by mistake, he looked ready to cut my life short on the spot.

[P135]
“We’re part of the orthodox faction.”

[P136]
“Are you? Then why are you stammering?”

[P137]
“I’m telling the truth.”

[P138]
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan… I feel like I’ve heard of it. Or perhaps I haven’t.”

[P139]
Jeok Cheongang sank deep into thought, then suddenly gave me a peculiar look.

[P140]
“The more I look at you, the stranger you seem. That thing just now—it was you, wasn’t it?”

[P141]
*That thing just now?*

[P142]
His words were vague, but I immediately understood.

[P143]
*This old man definitely sensed Qi Sense.*

[P144]
*How is that possible?*

[P145]
I had vaguely suspected as much when he reacted right away, but the realization still made my vision go dark.

[P146]
*Good God. A monster who can sense Qi Sense.*

[P147]
“Why aren’t you answering?”

[P148]
I bit down hard on my lower lip.

[P149]
“No.”

[P150]
“How do you know what I’m talking about?”

[P151]
“…”

[P152]
“Hey. It was you, wasn’t it?”

[P153]
“No. Anyway, it wasn’t me.”

[P154]
“Oh, I like that. You’ve got some backbone. Very manly.”

[P155]
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily, then continued,

[P156]
“Should I break a few bones and ask again?”

[P157]
“It was me! Yes, it was me!”

[P158]
“Good. Then what did you do to me?”

[P159]
I hesitated.

[P160]
My opponent was an old man whose instincts were every bit as sharp as his age suggested. If I lied and got caught, I would not be leaving with my body intact.

[P161]
I needed to stick as closely to the truth as possible while phrasing it in a way he would find agreeable.

[P162]
“You seemed like an extraordinary person, so I just…”

[P163]
“Just what?”

[P164]
“I checked whether you had learned martial arts.”

[P165]
“How?”

[P166]
“Yes?”

[P167]
“I asked how you did it.”

[P168]
“I sent a little of my qi toward you and read yours. Something like that.”

[P169]
“Ha. Is that so?”

[P170]
Jeok Cheongang laughed as though amused, then clenched his fist.

[P171]
“If you keep lying, I’ll break your legs. Answer me again.”

[P172]
I hurriedly waved my hands.

[P173]
“W-Wait. Why are you suddenly acting like this?”

[P174]
“You’ve misjudged this old man. Do I look like some fool who can’t tell the difference? What I felt just now… was different. Different enough to make me think it was some kind of dark art.”

[P175]
“What dark art? I’m telling you the truth!”

[P176]
*This is driving me insane.*

[P177]
Qi Sense was admittedly a cheat Skill, closer to a System function than martial arts.

[P178]
Because of that, someone like Jeok Cheongang, who appeared to be a Supreme Peak master, might have sensed something alien that he had never encountered before.

[P179]
*The problem is, how the hell am I supposed to explain that?*

[P180]
“You bastard! Tell me the truth!”

[P181]
*Fuck this. I’m done.*

[P182]
I decided to lay everything out honestly.

[P183]
“The truth is, I use something called the System. It’s a bit of a cheat, so it might have felt strange to you. I’m sorry.”

[P184]
Jeok Cheongang remained silent for a moment.

[P185]
Then he opened his mouth.

[P186]
“What kind of bullshit is that?”

[P187]
“…I told you exactly what happened. I figured you wouldn’t understand.”

[P188]
“Have you said all you have to say?”

[P189]
“There’s plenty I haven’t said. I’ve been through a lot.”

[P190]
“You’ve led a turbulent life.”

[P191]
“You have no idea.”

[P192]
“Don’t worry. After today, your life won’t have any more twists and turns.”

[P193]
“Are you planning to make it all downhill from here?”

[P194]
“Isn’t it obvious? Shall we start by warming you up a little?”

[P195]
It happened in an instant—too fast for me, Cheongpung, Hyuk Mujin, or Jang Taebo to react.

[P196]
Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh and poked me in the chest with one finger.

[P197]
And then…

[P198]
Fwoosh!

[P199]
An overwhelming wave of heat swept through my body.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

“We’re part of the orthodox faction.”

[P136]
“Are you? Then why are you stammering?”

[P137]
“I’m telling the truth.”

[P138]
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan… I feel like I’ve heard of it. Or perhaps I haven’t.”

[P139]
Jeok Cheongang sank deep into thought, then suddenly gave me a peculiar look.

[P140]
“The more I look at you, the stranger you seem. That thing just now—it was you, wasn’t it?”

[P141]
*That thing just now?*

[P142]
His words were vague, but I immediately understood.

[P143]
*This old man definitely sensed Qi Sense.*

[P144]
*How is that possible?*

[P145]
I had vaguely suspected as much when he reacted right away, but the realization still made my vision go dark.

[P146]
*Good God. A monster who can sense Qi Sense.*

[P147]
“Why aren’t you answering?”

[P148]
I bit down hard on my lower lip.

[P149]
“No.”

[P150]
“How do you know what I’m talking about?”

[P151]
“…”

[P152]
“Hey. It was you, wasn’t it?”

[P153]
“No. Anyway, it wasn’t me.”

[P154]
“Oh, I like that. You’ve got some backbone. Very manly.”

[P155]
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily, then continued,

[P156]
“Should I break a few bones and ask again?”

[P157]
“It was me! Yes, it was me!”

[P158]
“Good. Then what did you do to me?”

[P159]
I hesitated.

[P160]
My opponent was an old man whose instincts were every bit as sharp as his age suggested. If I lied and got caught, I would not be leaving with my body intact.

[P161]
I needed to stick as closely to the truth as possible while phrasing it in a way he would find agreeable.

[P162]
“You seemed like an extraordinary person, so I just…”

[P163]
“Just what?”

[P164]
“I checked whether you had learned martial arts.”

[P165]
“How?”

[P166]
“Yes?”

[P167]
“I asked how you did it.”

[P168]
“I sent a little of my qi toward you and read yours. Something like that.”

[P169]
“Ha. Is that so?”

[P170]
Jeok Cheongang laughed as though amused, then clenched his fist.

[P171]
“If you keep lying, I’ll break your legs. Answer me again.”

[P172]
I hurriedly waved my hands.

[P173]
“W-Wait. Why are you suddenly acting like this?”

[P174]
“You’ve misjudged this old man. Do I look like some fool who can’t tell the difference? What I felt just now… was different. Different enough to make me think it was some kind of dark art.”

[P175]
“What dark art? I’m telling you the truth!”

[P176]
*This is driving me insane.*

[P177]
Qi Sense was admittedly a cheat Skill, closer to a System function than martial arts.

[P178]
Because of that, someone like Jeok Cheongang, who appeared to be a Supreme Peak master, might have sensed something alien that he had never encountered before.

[P179]
*The problem is, how the hell am I supposed to explain that?*

[P180]
“You bastard! Tell me the truth!”

[P181]
*Fuck this. I’m done.*

[P182]
I decided to lay everything out honestly.

[P183]
“The truth is, I use something called the System. It’s a bit of a cheat, so it might have felt strange to you. I’m sorry.”

[P184]
Jeok Cheongang remained silent for a moment.

[P185]
Then he opened his mouth.

[P186]
“What kind of bullshit is that?”

[P187]
“…I told you exactly what happened. I figured you wouldn’t understand.”

[P188]
“Have you said all you have to say?”

[P189]
“There’s plenty I haven’t said. I’ve been through a lot.”

[P190]
“You’ve led a turbulent life.”

[P191]
“You have no idea.”

[P192]
“Don’t worry. After today, your life won’t have any more twists and turns.”

[P193]
“Are you planning to make it all downhill from here?”

[P194]
“Isn’t it obvious? Shall we start by warming you up a little?”

[P195]

[P196]

[P197]

[P198]
Fwoosh!

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

[P91]
The next moment, something unknown shot toward him from behind.

[P92]
Whoosh.

[P93]
He could neither see nor hear it.

[P94]
He merely felt it—a cold, unfamiliar presence closing in on his back.

[P95]
*An ambush?*

[P96]
No. He sensed none of the sticky, unpleasant killing intent that accompanied one.

[P97]
Instead, it felt as natural as a breeze blowing from afar, which only made it more alien.

[P98]
The unknown energy vanished the moment it touched Jeok Cheongang’s back.

[P99]
*What in the world…?*

[P100]
He had lived for nearly a hundred years, yet this was the first time he had ever experienced anything like it.

[P101]
Still bewildered, he turned around and immediately identified the culprit.

[P102]
“Looks like you were just barking up the wrong tree…”

[P103]
The young man’s mouth snapped shut the instant their eyes met. His gaze wavered, and his fingertips twitched.

[P104]
As Jeok Cheongang stared at the culprit, the corners of his mouth slowly rose.

[P105]
“Well, now…”

[P106]
He stroked his chin, intrigued.

[P107]
“What an interesting fellow.”

[P108]
At the same time, his foot pushed off the ground.

[P109]
In the next instant, the distance of more than ten jang between them vanished. Jeok Cheongang whispered into Jin Taekyung’s ear.

[P110]
* * *

[P111]
*Inventory summon.*

[P112]
Just six syllables.

[P113]
All I had to do was picture the spear and shout the words in my mind. But…

[P114]
“What are you?”

[P115]
The breath tickling the back of my neck made every hair on my body stand on end.

[P116]
*When did he—?*

[P117]
No, before that…

[P118]
*How?*

[P119]
*He was definitely, definitely Level 3.*

[P120]
It was impossible to believe.

[P121]
Jeok Cheongang looked as though he could drop dead at any moment, yet he was faster than anyone I had ever seen.

[P122]
So fast that I did not even dare consider resisting him.

[P123]
“Hey. When an elder asks you a question, you’re supposed to answer.”

[P124]
“Y-Yes?”

[P125]
“You call that an answer?”

[P126]
A thin, wrinkled finger repeatedly poked me in the solar plexus. There was no force or internal energy behind it, yet it felt as though someone were stabbing me with a sword.

[P127]
“I’m asking what you are.”

[P128]
I swallowed hard. My mouth felt as dry as if someone had poured a handful of sand into it.

[P129]
“I’m Jin Taekyung.”

[P130]
“Not that crap. Which sect are you a disciple of?”

[P131]
“Taiyuan—the Jin Family of Taiyuan.”

[P132]
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan? Are you one of those demonic, heterodox sorts?”

[P133]
I nearly nodded without thinking.

[P134]
The old man’s eyes had flashed when he mentioned demonic, heterodox arts. If I said yes even by mistake, he looked ready to cut my life short on the spot.

[P135]
“We’re part of the orthodox faction.”

[P136]
“Are you? Then why are you stammering?”

[P137]
“I’m telling the truth.”

[P138]
“The Jin Family of Taiyuan… I feel like I’ve heard of it. Or perhaps I haven’t.”

[P139]
Jeok Cheongang sank deep into thought, then suddenly gave me a peculiar look.

[P140]
“The more I look at you, the stranger you seem. That thing just now—it was you, wasn’t it?”

[P141]
*That thing just now?*

[P142]
His words were vague, but I immediately understood.

[P143]
*This old man definitely sensed Qi Sense.*

[P144]
*How is that possible?*

[P145]
I had vaguely suspected as much when he reacted right away, but the realization still made my vision go dark.

[P146]
*Good God. A monster who can sense Qi Sense.*

[P147]
“Why aren’t you answering?”

[P148]
I bit down hard on my lower lip.

[P149]
“No.”

[P150]
“How do you know what I’m talking about?”

[P151]
“…”

[P152]
“Hey. It was you, wasn’t it?”

[P153]
“No. Anyway, it wasn’t me.”

[P154]
“Oh, I like that. You’ve got some backbone. Very manly.”

[P155]
Jeok Cheongang laughed heartily, then continued,

[P156]
“Should I break a few bones and ask again?”

[P157]
“It was me! Yes, it was me!”

[P158]
“Good. Then what did you do to me?”

[P159]
I hesitated.

[P160]
My opponent was an old man whose instincts were every bit as sharp as his age suggested. If I lied and got caught, I would not be leaving with my body intact.

[P161]
I needed to stick as closely to the truth as possible while phrasing it in a way he would find agreeable.

[P162]
“You seemed like an extraordinary person, so I just…”

[P163]
“Just what?”

[P164]
“I checked whether you had learned martial arts.”

[P165]
“How?”

[P166]
“Yes?”

[P167]
“I asked how you did it.”

[P168]
“I sent a little of my qi toward you and read yours. Something like that.”

[P169]
“Ha. Is that so?”

[P170]
Jeok Cheongang laughed as though amused, then clenched his fist.

[P171]
“If you keep lying, I’ll break your legs. Answer me again.”

[P172]
I hurriedly waved my hands.

[P173]
“W-Wait. Why are you suddenly acting like this?”

[P174]
“You’ve misjudged this old man. Do I look like some fool who can’t tell the difference? What I felt just now… was different. Different enough to make me think it was some kind of dark art.”

[P175]
“What dark art? I’m telling you the truth!”

[P176]
*This is driving me insane.*

[P177]
Qi Sense was admittedly a cheat Skill, closer to a System function than martial arts.

[P178]
Because of that, someone like Jeok Cheongang, who appeared to be a Supreme Peak master, might have sensed something alien that he had never encountered before.

[P179]
*The problem is, how the hell am I supposed to explain that?*

[P180]
“You bastard! Tell me the truth!”

[P181]
*Fuck this. I’m done.*

[P182]
I decided to lay everything out honestly.

[P183]
“The truth is, I use something called the System. It’s a bit of a cheat, so it might have felt strange to you. I’m sorry.”

[P184]
Jeok Cheongang remained silent for a moment.

[P185]
Then he opened his mouth.

[P186]
“What kind of bullshit is that?”

[P187]
“…I told you exactly what happened. I figured you wouldn’t understand.”

[P188]
“Have you said all you have to say?”

[P189]
“There’s plenty I haven’t said. I’ve been through a lot.”

[P190]
“You’ve led a turbulent life.”

[P191]
“You have no idea.”

[P192]
“Don’t worry. After today, your life won’t have any more twists and turns.”

[P193]
“Are you planning to make it all downhill from here?”

[P194]
“Isn’t it obvious? Shall we start by warming you up a little?”

[P195]
It happened in an instant—too fast for me, Cheongpung, Hyuk Mujin, or Jang Taebo to react.

[P196]
Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh and poked me in the chest with one finger.

[P197]
And then…

[P198]
Fwoosh!

[P199]
An overwhelming wave of heat swept through my body.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.

- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
